quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right of way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow showed. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming and tells you to reduce your speed.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: On a road with three or more lanes, when must you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?

options.text: If you are traveling in either direction.
If you are traveling toward the bus.
Only if children are crossing the road.
Only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.
questions.explanation: On a road with three or more lanes or a road divided by a median, you do not have to stop for a school bus if it is traveling in the opposite direction. You must stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's weight pulls it straight, which makes turning difficult. To stay in control, you must slow down before entering a curve.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Rely on your mirrors.
Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can be hidden in your blind spot. Glance over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet in advance on residential streets and five seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Follow other vehicles more closely.
Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, do not make sudden changes in speed or direction. Reduce your speed and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: By law, when must your vehicle's headlights be on?

options.text: One hour after sunset until one hour before sunrise.
One hour before sunset until one hour after sunrise.
30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
30 minutes before sunset until 30 minutes after sunrise.

questions.correctAnswerText: 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: Your headlights must be on from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.

questions.question: Which way is the safest way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve and gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up as you enter a curve makes your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: Smoked marijuana and marijuana-infused foods:

options.text: Have the same risks.
Have different risks.
Have minimal side effects when mixed with alcohol.
Will not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have different risks.
questions.explanation: Marijuana-infused foods affect you more slowly than smoked marijuana. Smoking marijuana can damage your lungs. Any form of marijuana can impair your driving ability.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park your car.
Places where you must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Only cross when you are certain it is safe.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when visibility is reduced or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopping?

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front when stopped on an uphill slope. The vehicle ahead might roll backward when traffic moves. Extra space reduces the chance of a collision.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Press your brakes hard.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, the vehicle will keep going. Turn off the ignition carefully—move it just enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Follow the car ahead more closely.
Stay farther behind the car ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Go through slowly and carefully.
Get ready to stop because the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go through the intersection slowly and with caution. Look both ways before crossing.

questions.question: What is the first thing to adjust when you get in a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt.
The steering wheel.
Your rearview mirror.
Your seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat.
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped off the road with no flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop no matter which side of the road you are on.
Stop until the bus driver signals you to go.
Stop only if you are on the same side of the road as the bus.
Pass carefully because you do not have to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully because you do not have to stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with red flashing lights whether you are on the same side, opposite side, or approaching at an intersection. If the lights are not flashing and the stop arm is not out, you may pass with caution.

questions.question: What type of sign has this shape and color?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are used only to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: When must you pull over to let an emergency vehicle pass?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the lane that has the broken line.

questions.question: If you need to stop fast and your car does not have Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down hard and hold it.
Pump the brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. It helps you stop fast and still steer the car.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on white. They tell drivers what they must or must not do, such as speed limits or no passing rules.
